description: Bars grouped side by side or stacked, with optional line overlays.

data.rainfallAria: Average monthly rainfall in London, Tokyo and Paris

data.rankingAria: Online sales by country, from highest to lowest
data.targetAria: New customers per week against the weekly target
data.drillHint: Click a quarter to see its months.
data.quarterDetail: {{quarter}}: {{value}} in total. Click a month for its revenue.
data.quartersAria: Revenue per quarter in 2026; click a quarter to see its months

props.name: series
props.description: Series drawn as bars unless they set a `type` (e.g. a `line` overlay)

props.name: stacked
props.description: Stacks the bars of every series (otherwise they are grouped side by side)

props.name: percent
props.description: Scales the stacks to 100% (implies `stacked`)

props.name: labels
props.description: Writes the value above every bar

props.name: orientation
props.description: `horizontal` draws the bars from the left, the categories down the left side

props.name: tooltip
props.description: Tooltip; `false` disables it

props.name: legend
props.description: Legend; shown by default when several series have a name

props.name: height
props.description: Height of the chart (the legend included); numbers are pixels

props.name: width
props.description: Width of the chart; numbers are pixels

props.name: renderTooltip
props.description: React content of the tooltip (replaces the default content)

props.name: xAxis
props.description: X axis

props.name: yAxis
props.description: Y axis

props.name: renderer
props.description: Backend of the data layer: `auto` tries WebGPU, then WebGL2, then WebGL, then Canvas2D

props.name: crosshair
props.description: Vertical guide line following the pointer

props.name: annotations
props.description: Background areas and reference lines

props.name: interaction
props.description: Zoom (Ctrl / ⌘ + wheel, pinch), pan (drag), double-click reset and keyboard navigation; `false` makes the chart static

props.name: padding
props.description: Space around the plot area, in pixels

props.name: palette
props.description: Series colors (defaults to the `--chart-series-1..8` CSS variables, then the theme colors)

props.name: ariaLabel
props.description: Accessible name of the chart

props.name: locale
props.description: Locale of the texts and numbers the chart writes (tooltip rows, compact units `k` / `万`, separators, month and weekday names of time axes)

events.name: onPointClick
events.description: Called when a point (or bar) is clicked

events.name: onPlotClick
events.description: Called when the plot area is clicked where there is no point

events.name: onHover
events.description: Called when the hovered (or keyboard-focused) points change

events.name: onZoom
events.description: Called when the user zooms or pans

events.name: onRendererChange
events.description: Called with the backend once it is ready (and when it falls back after a GPU loss)

BarChartProps.description: Props of BarChart (`labels` writes the values: override the tooltip texts with `tooltip.labels`)

examples.title: Basic
examples.description: One series of [category, value] tuples; the y axis always includes zero.

examples.title: Bars and line
examples.description: A series with type: "line" is drawn over the bars, here a 7-day average.

examples.title: Deployments over time
examples.description: Stacked bars on a time axis count the successful and rolled-back deployments of each day; rect annotations shade the weekends and a change freeze, and a summary gives the deployment frequency and change failure rate.

examples.title: Drill down
examples.description: onPointClick on a quarter swaps the series for its three months, and a Button brings the quarters back; clicking a month writes its revenue in an aria-live output.

examples.title: Cheapest hours to charge
examples.description: Tomorrow's hourly electricity prices, split into three stacked series so that each bar takes the color of its price tier. A rect annotation follows the cheapest run of hours for the charging time picked in the Select, and the output compares its cost with charging on arrival.

examples.title: Grouped
examples.description: Several series without stacked sit side by side in each category, here the monthly rainfall of three cities; Intl.NumberFormat writes the unit.

examples.title: Value labels
examples.description: labels writes the value above every bar, with the y axis format, and leaves room for it above the tallest bar. Best with few bars, when exact values matter.

examples.title: 100% stacked
examples.description: percent scales every stack to 100% to compare the composition of groups of different sizes; the tooltip shows the number of answers and their share.

examples.title: Compare with last year
examples.description: A Switch sets hidden on last year's series to show or hide the comparison without changing the colors, and renderTooltip lists both years with the change in percent.

examples.title: Profit and loss
examples.description: Negative values grow downwards from zero; each datum sets its own color, green for a profit and red for a loss, and the y format shows the sign.

examples.title: Ranking
examples.description: Sort the data before passing it to rank the categories; Intl.DisplayNames gives the country names in the reader's language and showLabels writes the values.

examples.title: Stacked
examples.description: stacked piles the series on top of each other.

examples.title: Against a target
examples.description: A dashed y line marks the weekly target and the bars that reach it are highlighted through their datum color.

props.height: Height of the chart, the legend included: pixels or any CSS length
props.options: Other engine options (axes, legend, tooltip, palette, format…) merged with the element's own properties; property only
props.instance: The engine instance (minerva-design/charts/core), null until the element is rendered and connected

events.minerva-hover: The hovered (or keyboard-focused) points changed; detail: { x, xLabel, items }, null when nothing is hovered
events.minerva-point-click: A point or a bar was clicked; detail: { x, xLabel, items }
events.minerva-plot-click: The plot area was clicked where there is no point; detail: { x, y } in data coordinates
events.minerva-zoom: The user zoomed or panned; detail: { x, y } (the visible ranges)
events.minerva-renderer-change: The backend is ready, or fell back after a GPU loss; detail: { renderer }

methods.getView: Visible range, null before the engine is created
methods.getRenderer: Backend in use (webgpu, webgl2, webgl, canvas2d), null until ready
